purpose: Make the single accumulative incremental candidate a physical machine-enforced authority rather than a rule distributed across block locks and guard status enums.

rootCause.summary: The project required one accumulative candidate, but physical product composition authorization was distributed across Control Plane, B1/B2 locks, historical successor scopes and hardcoded status lists in the guard/workflow. A legitimate new remediation state could therefore make the guard ignore already-authorized product owners and report false source drift. This also made preservation of prior improvements dependent on multiple consumers staying manually synchronized.

demonstratedFailure.head: 577d455c618fa15614865f4f53832f79f00a210b
demonstratedFailure.discriminant: B2 lock authorized the causal owners, but guard b2Active did not recognize status OPEN_PAULA_VISUAL_REJECTED_REMEDIATION_REQUIRED, so the B2 allowed set was omitted.
demonstratedFailure.effect: The current cumulative source could not be certified even though the causal B2 owners were already physically authorized.

definitiveSolution.updateRule: Any product-source change must update this composition lock in the same atomic commit; otherwise the central guard fails closed before build/Preview.
definitiveSolution.noPreauthorization: A path may not remain in the composition manifest if it does not physically differ from the certified baseline.
definitiveSolution.noSilentOmission: Every physical product path that differs from the certified baseline must exist in this manifest.
definitiveSolution.blobBinding: Every listed path is bound to its current Git blob SHA.
definitiveSolution.statusLabelIndependence: Composition authorization does not depend on duplicated display/workflow status enums.
definitiveSolution.preservation: Prior accepted B1 improvements and all B2 causal fixes remain in one tree; no historical module package or overlay can replace the accumulated tree.
